items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes with the staged Ps tools (sweep.py --skel with --tokens, collate.py, verse_map_oshb.json, pmarks_Ps.json); Ps 149 and Ps 104 are identity psalms in web_mt_offset_map.json, so web:Ps.149.N = oshb:Ps.149.N and web:Ps.104.17 = oshb:Ps.104.17, and the row's refs stand in the right space. (1) COUNT OBJECT. The filed digit reproduces ONLY as the contiguous consonantal substring חסיד at skeleton tier: 26 verses / 26 tokens book-wide. It does not reproduce for the object the sentence names. The two named forms, חֲסִידִֽים (oshb:Ps.149.1, byte tier) and חֲסִידִ֣ים (oshb:Ps.149.5, byte tier) for chasidim and חֲסִידָ֗יו (oshb:Ps.149.9, byte tier) for chasidav, sweep at skeleton tier as חסידים = 2 verses (MT 149:1, 149:5) and חסידיו = 8 verses (MT 30:5, 31:24, 37:28, 85:9, 97:10, 116:15, 148:14, 149:9), 10 verses in all, exactly as the auditor filed. The 16-verse remainder (MT 4:4, 12:2, 16:10, 18:26, 32:6, 43:1, 50:5, 52:11, 79:2, 86:2, 89:20, 104:17, 132:9, 132:16, 145:10, 145:17; re-derived list identical to the finding's) is other inflections of the saints-noun in 15 verses plus, at MT 104:17, חֲ֝סִידָ֗ה (oshb:Ps.104.17, byte tier), the stork, “The stork makes its home in the cypress trees.” (web:Ps.104.17), a different lexeme caught by the contained substring, the very class the toolkit's sweep hazard catalog names as the contained-substring trap. So under the most charitable reading (the saints-noun in every inflection) the honest digit is 25 verses; under the reading the wording invites (the two named forms) it is 10; it is 26 under no reading of the words the saints-term, and the label skeleton tier names a collation level, not a licence to count a broader object than the one named (strategy section 10 count-object discipline: every count names WHAT it counts). Tested against the row: this is not a true claim lacking its digit but a digit bound to the wrong object, so the E-05 lane law yields medium, not low. (2) LOAD-BEARING TEST, seam 149:4|5 weighed from both sides. The preceding unit closes at MT 149:4 כִּֽי רוֹצֶ֣ה יְהוָ֣ה … עֲ֝נָוִ֗ים בִּישׁוּעָֽה (oshb:Ps.149.4, byte tier), a causal grounding clause with no ruled closer: Psalm 149 carries no Selah verse (the word-bound Selah inventory is 71 verses book-wide, none in Psalm 149), no refrain, and no K/Q note (pmarks_Ps.json kq: none in Psalm 149, none at MT 104:17), while the hallelu-Yah frame stands only at the psalm's edges, הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ verse-initial at oshb:Ps.149.1 and הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ verse-final at oshb:Ps.149.9 (byte tier). The following unit opens at MT 149:5 יַעְלְז֣וּ חֲסִידִ֣ים … עַל מִשְׁכְּבוֹתָֽם (oshb:Ps.149.5, byte tier), continuing the yod-preformative jussive chain that runs from יִשְׂמַ֣ח (oshb:Ps.149.2, byte tier) through 149:5; the only mood shifts in the psalm fall at 149:1|2 (the imperative שִׁ֣ירוּ of oshb:Ps.149.1 giving way to jussives) and at 149:6|7 (the infinitive-construct chain לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת oshb:Ps.149.7, לֶאְסֹ֣ר oshb:Ps.149.8, לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת oshb:Ps.149.9, all byte tier). The governing rule that decides is therefore that no tier-1 device stands on either side of 149:4|5: the seam is a discourse turn in setting only, which is exactly the posture the shipped row and its paired row M8-Ps-491 (Ps.149.5-Ps.149.9) both hold at medium with the whole_psalm rival live; the seam pair is coherent and this item does not touch it. The row's 3-of-3 recurrence claim is byte-TRUE (חֲסִידִֽים oshb:Ps.149.1; חֲסִידִ֣ים oshb:Ps.149.5; חֲסִידָ֗יו oshb:Ps.149.9; byte tier) and is what keeps the rival live; the book-wide digit only contextualizes it. Correcting the digit to 25 leaves the argument unchanged, and correcting it to 10 would put 3 of the 10 book-wide verses inside Psalm 149 and make the rival MORE live, not less, so the digit cannot flip the seam and is not load-bearing: medium, not high. It is not low either: the same false digit-object pairing is carried three times in the row (strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals[3], device_notes) and mirrored on the paired 149:5-9 row (there as 2 of 3 Psalm 149 members; 26 verses book-wide, where the 2-of-3 is likewise byte-true), so any cure is a seam-pair cure. (3) REPAIR PROPOSAL validated from bytes. Option A (rename the object to match 26 and disclose the stork) is byte-sound only if the object is named as the consonantal string חסיד swept as a contained substring, not as the saints-root: 26 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, of which 25 carry the saints-noun and 1 (MT 104:17) the stork. Option B (keep the two named forms and correct the digit to 10 verses book-wide) is byte-sound as re-swept (2 + 8, with all three Psalm 149 members inside those two forms). A third byte-sound wording is the saints-noun in every inflection, 25 verses book-wide at skeleton tier, excluding the homographic stork at MT 104:17 (token-by-token classification of the 26 hits: 7 singular, 2 plural absolute, 16 suffixed, 1 stork). Each remains a PROPOSAL for owner triage, to be installed identically on M8-Ps-490 and M8-Ps-491; span_change is false, so span_ruling is n/a. Verdict: confirm at medium (E-05 count-object overclaim). Same-model-family corroboration of the auditor's re-sweep, not independent confirmation.
